To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we have developed a novel, distributed, scalable, and responsive visualization system for large datasets that is capable of constructing visualizations from data stored in compressed columnar data stores, 2) we have implemented this system and compared it to three other systems for visualizations from data, and 3) the performance of our system is superior in most cases.
our system is able to build visualizations in real time and with guaranteed responsiveness, and that it is able to do this with a significant speed-up over the state of the art.
we have created a novel method for incrementally visualizing large datasets in a MapReduce framework that outperforms three popular data warehouse solutions in terms of both speed and responsiveness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of efficiently building visualizations of large datasets.
the problem of building information visualization from large datasets in a responsive and efficient manner.
the design and implementation of a system that can efficiently and incrementally construct visualizations of large data sets in a distributed environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is the fastest and most responsive method for visualizing large data sets.
our method allows for a more responsive and faster end-to-end visualization of very large datasets than other systems that we have tested.
our method outperforms all three other systems by at least an order of magnitude, and in many cases by several orders of magnitude, in terms of speed, responsiveness and memory consumption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a method for incremental computation of visualizations in a MapReduce-style algorithm, and show that our method is faster than querying three other database and data warehouse solutions for building visualizations.
we have developed a system that can be used for exploratory data analytics of large datasets, and that is able to handle the complexity of the data, and the complexity of the user interaction.
VisReduce is a fast and responsive system for incremental visualization construction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a distributed columnar data store with an incremental MapReduce-like algorithm can be used to build visualizations of large datasets with high responsiveness.
a distributed system for visual analytics can be implemented in a way that is responsive, scalable, and efficient.
a MapReduce-style algorithm combined with a compressed column-oriented data store is an effective and efficient way of incrementally building visualizations of large datasets.
